headline: Nearly eight in ten Americans want AI companies to slow down or stop building powerful AI until its safety is checked, a Quinnipiac poll finds.
score_reason: Lowered 2 from the pool score 6: the poll was released on 30 Sep and already ran in our 1 Oct edition (item 129); only extra results are new.
importance_line: A public that leans towards caution matters first to voters and communities, then to lawmakers deciding on AI rules, then to AI companies, but it is a single poll (margin of error 3.5 points) measuring opinion, not whether any harm will occur.
summary: Quinnipiac University reports that in its poll of 1,202 US adults, taken 24 to 27 September, 47% want AI companies in the US to slow down, and 30% to stop, developing powerful AI until its safety can be evaluated, while 5% want them to move faster. The poll was released on 30 September and we carried it in our 1 Oct edition; this entry adds its findings on the pace of AI development, which The Decoder reported on 5 Oct.
notes: Repeat of our 1 Oct item 129 (same poll release, same url): hold back as old news re-dated unless the pace-of-development results are wanted. Read The Decoder and the Quinnipiac release in full.
